title: Branch, indirect call and branch-free selection under constant, alternating and random targets
question: Choosing one of two operations per call, how does the cost of a conditional branch to direct calls, an indirect call through a run-time table, the same indirect call preceded by a correlated conditional branch, and branch-free arithmetic depend on how predictable the selector is, and is any difference explained by extra instructions, mispredictions, or what the predictors can see?
design_target: AMD Ryzen 3 7330U (family 19h, model 50h, Zen 3), Linux 7.0.0-42 with spectre_v2 'Retpolines; IBPB conditional; IBRS_FW; STIBP always-on' (read from sysfs, never changed).

placements.name: measured-cpu
placements.meaning: the single measured thread on CPU 2; its SMT sibling CPU 3 is not reserved and its busy fraction is recorded per row

ex_ret_instr.justification: perf list (amdzen3): Retired Instructions; the generic PERF_COUNT_HW_INSTRUCTIONS on family 19h (0x00c0, amd_zen2_perfmon_event_map, arch/x86/events/amd/core.c, Linux v7.0; sysfs events/instructions). A mechanism's instructions per call must not change with the distribution.

ls_not_halted_cyc.justification: perf list: Cycles not in Halt; the generic PERF_COUNT_HW_CPU_CYCLES on family 19h (0x0076).

ex_ret_brn.justification: perf list: Retired Branch Instructions; the generic PERF_COUNT_HW_BRANCH_INSTRUCTIONS on family 19h (0x00c2; sysfs events/branch-instructions).

ex_ret_brn_misp.justification: perf list: Retired Branch Instructions Mispredicted; the generic PERF_COUNT_HW_BRANCH_MISSES on family 19h (0x00c3; sysfs events/branch-misses).

ex_ret_brn_ind_misp.justification: perf list: Retired Indirect Branch Instructions Mispredicted; 'each such mispredict incurs the same penalty as a mispredicted conditional branch instruction; only EX mispredicts are counted'. Separates target mispredictions of the indirect call from direction mispredictions.

ex_ret_ind_brch_instr.justification: perf list: Retired Indirect Branch Instructions. One per call is expected for indirect and hinted, zero for branch and branchless (returns are counted separately).

bp_dyn_ind_pred.role: use of the dynamic indirect predictor
bp_dyn_ind_pred.justification: perf list: Dynamic Indirect Predictions. Shows whether the indirect call's predictions came from the history-based indirect predictor at all.

ex_ret_msprd_brnch_instr_dir_msmtch.justification: perf list: Retired Mispredicted Branch Instructions due to Direction Mismatch (event 0x1c7: config bits 0-7 = 0xc7, bits 32-35 = 0x1 by the PMU's sysfs format).

ex_ret_near_ret.justification: perf list: Retired Near Returns. One per call is expected wherever an operation is called.

ex_ret_near_ret_mispred.justification: perf list: Retired Near Returns Mispredicted. A control: returns are predicted by a return-address stack, so they should not depend on the selector.

bp_de_redirect.justification: perf list: Decode Redirects. A control for front-end redirects that are not execute-time mispredictions.

hypotheses.claim: Extra dispatch work: with a constant target every mechanism is predicted, and indirect differs from branch only by its instructions.
predictions: near-zero mispredictions per call for every mechanism under constant
branchless executes the fewest instructions and cycles per call
hypotheses.falsified_if: mispredictions per call are material under the constant distribution

hypotheses.claim: Misprediction cost: with random selectors both the conditional branch and the indirect call mispredict about half the calls, and each misprediction costs a pipeline restart; branch-free selection is insensitive to the distribution.
predictions: about 0.5 mispredictions per call for branch and indirect under random
their cycles per call rise accordingly
branchless cycles per call are equal across distributions
hypotheses.falsified_if: random selectors leave mispredictions or cycles per call unchanged

hypotheses.claim: History-based prediction learns a period-two pattern for both the conditional branch and the indirect call.
predictions: near-zero mispredictions per call for branch and indirect under alternating
hypotheses.falsified_if: either mechanism mispredicts materially under alternating

hypotheses.claim: Indirect targets are predicted from global branch history: the plain indirect call has no preceding conditional branch that correlates with its target, while hinted places one there.
predictions: hinted has near-zero indirect mispredictions under alternating and random
under random its conditional branch still mispredicts about half the calls
hypotheses.falsified_if: hinted still mispredicts its indirect target under alternating

hypotheses.claim: A mitigation (STIBP always-on, retpolines, IBPB) disables or limits user-space indirect prediction on this host.
predictions: indirect mispredictions persist whatever history precedes the call
hypotheses.falsified_if: hinted removes the indirect mispredictions; H5 cannot be tested further here because changing mitigations is a host-policy change

hypotheses.claim: Frequency or host noise produces the differences.
predictions: user cycles per ns differ between variants of a regime
hypotheses.falsified_if: cycle-based and time-based orderings agree with the same effective cycle rate

design_log: H1-H3 and the three original mechanisms were written first. A smoke run then showed the indirect call mispredicting about 99% of calls under the alternating distribution while the conditional branch mispredicted almost none. H3 is kept as written, and the hinted mechanism and H4/H5 were added to discriminate between missing history and a disabled predictor. The smoke runs are not evidence; only the gated runs are.
limits: One thread, user space only. The SMT sibling CPU 3 is not reserved: with STIBP always-on (sysfs) indirect-branch predictions are not shared between siblings, but the core's other front-end and execution resources are.
-fcf-protection (Ubuntu's default) adds endbr64 at every call target; the disassembly shows the actual code.
Two targets, three distributions and one call site are a bounded probe, not a characterization of the predictors.
